clue.text: Resigns from partnerships in writing

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen at the crease
something put down on paper is set down in writing

explanation.surface: Someone quits the firm's partnerships by sending a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket stand is a batting partnership between two players.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is a phrasal verb meaning to step away from a post or quit office.

clue.text: Like people's first charter?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word people's is taken

parts.note: to charter a boat is to hire or lease it

explanation.surface: A question about whether a founding document for the people would be popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is a verb here, as in 'do as you like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Do as you like and do as you please are the same: both verbs mean to wish or choose.

clue.text: Sent a Defoe novel, and one by Steinbeck

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or different, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone posts a Daniel Defoe book along with a John Steinbeck one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after Defoe's name, but it is the adjective signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck wrote this 1952 novel, later a James Dean film.

clue.text: Bank calling me away

indicators.note: away tells us the word me is sent off from the synonym

parts.note: a metier is one's trade or vocation, one's calling

explanation.surface: A bank phones a customer, but the customer is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of seats is a row or level, one layer rising above another.

clue.text: Club member in register managed to get one inside

parts.note: a rota is a list or register of duties

indicators.note: inside tells us one is placed within the word for managed

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives ran
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A member of a club is on the duty roster and manages to fit someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary International is a service club whose members carry this name.

clue.text: Opposed to substantial houses

indicators.note: houses as a verb means contains, so the letters sit within the word substantial

explanation.surface: Someone objects to big mansions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, the same as being opposed to something.

clue.text: Remain involved in Hitchcock film

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays on to work in an Alfred Hitchcock movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock directed this 1964 thriller starring Tippi Hedren and Sean Connery.

clue.text: Powerful state embracing the Spanish song

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the Spanish article sits within the other pieces

parts.note: hot can mean strong or powerful, as in a hot curry
California is a US state
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A mighty American state wraps its arms around a Spanish connection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eagles released this famous 1977 rock track.

clue.text: Show disapproval about Northern Ireland bishop's mock title

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hiss wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: an audience hisses to show disapproval
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: People jeer at a Belfast bishop's grandiose title.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of bishop's is a link meaning 'has', giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular honorific for a self-important person, a parody of 'His Excellency'.

clue.text: Star on the rocks? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a ship on the rocks is wrecked and sunk

explanation.surface: A star whose career or marriage has hit trouble, not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' also suggests a drink with ice, or a failing marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Our nearest star is the one around which Earth orbits.

clue.text: Conservative blocking amendment causes heated dispute

indicators.note: blocking means placed in the way, so the Conservative sits inside the amendment

parts.note: an amendment is an alteration or change
C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: A Tory MP blocking a bill change sparks a row in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or row, a heated argument.

clue.text: Problem children matter

definitions.meaning: a problem or concern, as in 'what is the problem?'
offspring, a legal sense as in 'died without children'
a subject under discussion, the topic or point

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a difficulty, offspring, and a topic for debate.

clue.text: Make a face? Brit, grotesquely

indicators.note: grotesquely means in a distorted way, so these letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A Briton pulls a hideous expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to construct or manufacture something, especially from parts.

clue.text: Autocratic leader runs into considerable trouble

parts.note: considerable means large or big

indicators.note: into tells us runs goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: bother is trouble or nuisance
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dictator gets into a lot of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's all-seeing ruler in Nineteen Eighty-Four is a byword for tyrannical surveillance.

clue.text: We, in refurbished snack bar, reply impertinently

indicators.note: in places the word We inside the reworked letters
refurbished means done up anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Staff in a revamped café give cheeky replies to customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' turns SNACK BAR into ANSRBACK, and 'in' puts WE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheeky or rude in response, especially to someone in authority.

clue.text: Ruined, stained across front of pants

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so stained goes around the picked letter

parts.note: soiled means dirtied or stained

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word pants

explanation.surface: Underpants dirtied at the front are ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoiled is damaged or wrecked beyond use.

clue.text: Praise article on socially acceptable male drug

parts.note: to laud is to praise
an is the indefinite article
U means upper-class, socially acceptable in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone praises a piece about a decent man's medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class versus non-upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium tincture once widely taken as a painkiller and sedative.

clue.text: Book is on units of heredity

indicators.note: on means the word is follows the units in an across answer

parts.note: genes are the units of heredity

explanation.surface: A book discusses genes.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Bible, telling the story of creation.

clue.text: Small notice over head brings sorrow

indicators.note: over means the first pieces sit above the headland in a down answer

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A little advertisement about a person's head causes grief.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS (as in Loch Ness or Dungeness) is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness and sorrow are synonyms for grief or unhappiness.

clue.text: Not a bona fide competitor in the arms race?

definitions.text: Not a bona fide competitor in the arms race?

parts.words: Not a bona fide competitor in the arms race?
parts.note: a runner is a competitor in a race, but this one runs guns: a smuggler of weapons, not a real racer

explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of firearms runs guns, so in an arms race this person is no real athlete.

clue.text: Heartless guy, pinching bottom, makes one cross

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing in, so the outer letters hold the bottom
heartless means the middle letter of guy is dropped, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the rump is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted man pinches someone's backside and makes them angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy and cross both mean bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: Foremost of directors study fear

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of directors

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: The chief of the board studies a fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread and fear are synonyms, both as nouns and verbs.

clue.text: Stop row involving Greek character

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the noise wraps round the letter

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a row
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A quarrel involving a Greek person is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is noise (rhymes with cow), not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to hold or stop them, as police do.

clue.text: In serious difficulty contending with Italian

parts.note: to be up against something is to be contending with it
It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble because they are taking on an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for facing great trouble with no easy way out.

clue.text: Leading parade miles away

indicators.note: away means the miles are taken off

parts.note: a parade is a march

explanation.surface: The front of the procession is miles off.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as a prefix-like adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-rival.

clue.text: Take this to heed short message

definitions.meaning: to take ... of something is to heed it
a brief written message, like a memo

explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the phrase 'take note', meaning pay attention, and is a brief letter.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase extra

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for purchase is spoken

parts.note: to buy is to purchase

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have bought something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is an extra: a run scored without the bat touching the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, extras include runs that come when the ball passes the batsman untouched.

clue.text: What one must do with litter to redeem a bad situation?

definitions.text: What one must do with litter
definitions.meaning: literally collecting broken bits of rubbish from the ground
figuratively restoring order after a disaster

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for recovering after a setback, and also the literal act of tidying up debris.
